BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                  OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI
 In the Matter of Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy   )
 Missouri Metro’s Request for Authority to          )       Case No. ER-2026-0143
 Implement a General Rate Increase for Electric     )
 Service

     ORDER DENYING MOTION TO STRIKE TESTIMONY AND GRANTING
             MOTION TO FILE RESPONSIVE SURREBUTTAL

Issue Date: October 1, 2026                                  Effective Date: October 1, 2026

       On September 23, 2026, Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Missouri Metro (Evergy

Metro) filed a motion asking the Commission to strike portions of the surrebuttal testimony

of the Office of the Public Counsel (Public Counsel) witnesses David Shapley and Paul

Alvarez. The portions of testimony Evergy Metro objects to address transmission cost

disallowances proposed by Public Counsel. In the alternative, Evergy Metro asks to file

responsive sur-surrebuttal.

       Evergy Metro states that Commission Rule 20 CSR 4240-2.130(7)(A), which requires

direct testimony to include all testimony and exhibits asserting and explaining that party’s

entire case in-chief’. Evergy Metro argues that Public Counsel failed to do so in violation of

the Commission’s rules. Evergy Metro asserts that Public Counsel, by making the request in

surrebuttal, prevented other parties from having a sufficient opportunity to conduct

discovery or provide responsive testimony.

       In its response to Evergy Metro’s motion to strike, Public Counsel states that Evergy

Metro unreasonably delayed providing Public Counsel related discovery information.
          When determining the appropriateness of a rate or charge that a utility seeks to have

its customers pay, the Commission is required to review and consider all relevant factors. 1

Transmission costs are a relevant factor in determining the appropriate rates for Evergy

Metro.

         Therefore, the Commission will deny Evergy Metro’s request to strike Public

Counsel’s transmission cost related testimony. However, the Commission will grant Evergy

Metro’s alternative request to file responsive sur-surrebuttal.

         THE COMMISSION ORDERS THAT:

         1.     Evergy Metro’s Motion to strike portions of the surrebuttal testimony of the

Public Counsel’s witnesses David Shapley and Paul Alvarez is denied.

         2.     Evergy Metro may file responsive sur-surrebuttal as attached to its motion.

         3.     This order is effective when issued.

                                                          BY THE COMMISSION




                                                          Nancy Dippell
                                                          Secretary

John T. Clark, Senior Regulatory Law Judge,
by delegation of authority pursuant to
Section 386.240, RSMo 2016.

Dated at Jefferson City, Missouri,
on this 1st day of October, 2026.
